headline: Southborough began planning for a projected FY28 budget deficit exceeding $2 million, refined Neary School renovation plans, and adopted health insurance negotiation rules.
synopsis: In August, Southborough municipal boards turned their attention toward fiscal pressures and upcoming Town Meeting business. Meeting jointly, the Select Board and Advisory Committee set FY28 budget instructions requiring departments to submit level-service and zero-growth budgets to confront a projected deficit exceeding $2 million. The Elementary School Building Committee advanced architectural options for Neary Elementary School, deciding to drop central district administration offices from future layouts and rejecting a 10-year phased repair strategy. The Select Board accepted state statutes allowing expedited collective negotiations on municipal health insurance plans and rejected an opt-out waiver, permitting licensed retail cannabis home delivery. Additionally, the Community Preservation Committee considered revised funding applications for golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge while deferring Fayville Memorial Park improvements to spring 2027.

top_items.title: Town prepares for projected FY28 budget deficit and potential override
top_items.why: Preliminary estimates show an operating deficit exceeding $2 million to maintain current municipal service levels. Departments were instructed to prepare both level-service and zero-growth budgets.
top_items.body: Meeting jointly with the Advisory Committee, the Select Board agreed on budget preparation instructions for department heads in anticipation of an FY28 structural deficit. Southborough entered the fiscal planning cycle with approximately $700,000 in excess levy capacity, while maintaining current service levels is projected to create a shortfall of more than $2 million. Departments must present two submissions: Budget A holding non-salary expenses flat to FY26 actuals, and Budget B showing no dollar increase over FY27 to demonstrate necessary reductions if an operating override is not sought.

top_items.title: Neary School building committee excludes district offices from design scope
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee instructed architects to remove central school district administration offices from future building plans and rejected a 10-year phased repair model.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects reviewed renovation and addition options for Neary Elementary School, including Option 4 featuring a new 13,000-square-foot east gymnasium and secure entry. Following discussions on space efficiency, the committee directed architects to drop the central school district administration offices from future design iterations. Members also dismissed a conceptual 10-year phased capital maintenance schedule, concluding that spreading construction over a decade would disrupt elementary classrooms without providing adequate educational enhancements ahead of a targeted March 2027 Town Meeting vote.

top_items.title: Select Board votes to enter health insurance reform negotiations
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 5-0 to adopt Massachusetts General Law Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23, enabling expedited negotiations with employee representatives over health insurance plans.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted unanimously to accept state statutes that allow the town to conduct expedited collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health plan designs. Employee health insurance accounts for 11.2 percent of the municipal operating budget. Because Northborough and the regional school district adopted the same statute, the three entities plan to align plan adjustments starting July 1, 2027, to mitigate rising healthcare premiums.

top_items.title: Adult-use marijuana home delivery allowed as opt-out fails
top_items.why: A motion to opt out of state regulations permitting adult-use marijuana home delivery failed 1-4 before the Select Board, leaving delivery allowed in Southborough.
top_items.body: The Select Board debated whether to adopt a municipal opt-out waiver against state regulations allowing licensed commercial marijuana retailers to deliver products directly to Southborough homes. Board members observed that only 13 of 154 eligible Massachusetts communities had opted out, and a motion to execute the opt-out failed on a 1-4 vote. Licensed courier delivery of adult-use cannabis products will therefore be permitted to residents aged 21 and older.

top_items.title: CPA funding requests revised for golf course irrigation and trails
top_items.why: Committees adjusted CPA funding requests for golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge, while the Fayville Memorial Park project was postponed.
top_items.body: The Golf Course Committee and DPW submitted an updated CPA application increasing the golf course irrigation budget to $1,087,296, requiring an additional $433,546 in CPA funds alongside a $100,000 contribution from the Golf Revolving Fund. The Trails Committee also narrowed its Peninsula Trail Phase II scope to an engineered pedestrian footbridge totaling $466,628, seeking $210,796 in new CPA funds while repurposing prior balances. Separately, the Recreation Commission announced plans to withdraw the Harold E. Fay Memorial Park funding article from the fall Special Town Meeting warrant to refine parking designs and await federal grant decisions ahead of Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Town boards review zoning amendments for two-family dwellings
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Board reviewed draft zoning amendments that would remove the requirement for a home to exist for two years before converting into a two-family dwelling.
top_items.body: The Zoning Board of Appeals hosted a public forum and the Planning Board examined proposed warrant language updating two-family dwelling rules for Special Town Meeting. The draft amendment repeals an existing condition requiring a structure to stand for at least two years prior to conversion into a two-family home, refines duplex and townhouse definitions, and preserves special permit oversight across zoning districts. Discussions addressed how the proposal interacts with industrial zoning districts, accessory dwelling units, and overall lot coverage limits.

top_items.title: Select Board authorizes $1 million MWRA loan for waterline looping
top_items.why: The board approved applying for an interest-free MWRA loan to connect dead-end water mains under the CSX railroad tracks.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted to endorse an application for a $1 million interest-free loan from the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority to fund the Presidential Drive and Fisher Road waterline looping project. The planned work connects two existing dead-end mains by boring underneath the CSX railroad tracks, improving neighborhood water pressure and reducing water stagnation. Officials noted that securing the interest-free loan will save the town more than $400,000 compared to conventional borrowing.
